classification.difficultyReason: Requires constructing auxiliary parallel lines and combining several angle relationships across a zigzag.

spec.description: Connected four-vertex zigzag with a right-angle square, 110° and 115° givens, unknown alpha, and matching single parallel marks on the terminal lines. Ordinary source-blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The terminal lines are parallel. Consecutive marked interior angles are 90°, 110°, 115° and alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=95^\circ$.

Construct auxiliary parallels and use corresponding and alternate angles.
answer.worked:
Through the first peak draw a line parallel to the terminal lines. Its angle with the segment leading back to the right-angle vertex is $90^\circ$, so the remaining part of the $110^\circ$ angle is $20^\circ$.

Through the second trough draw another parallel to the terminal lines. The angle between its upward ray and the segment leading back to the first peak is $20^\circ$ by alternate angles. The remaining part of the $115^\circ$ angle is therefore $95^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=115^\circ-(110^\circ-90^\circ)\\\alpha&=95^\circ\end{align*}$$
The last equality uses alternate angles between the auxiliary parallel and the right terminal line.
